en:
אָרַע (√רע, see רעע) to strike against. Nifal נֶאֱרַע to come in contact with (compare זווג), to happen, befall (genitive of evil occurrences). Berakhot IV, 2 שלא תֵּאָרַע וכ׳ (Bavli ed. 28ᵇ שלא יֵאָרַע דבר וכ׳) that no (religious) offence may happen through me (by an erroneous decision &c.). Yoma I, 1 שׁמא יארע בו פסול lest something may occur to him to unfit him for services. Esther Rabbah to II, 7 שיארע על ישראל (read שיארע לישר׳) will happen to Israel; and from

Piël - אֵירַע, אִירַע to strike, befall; (neut. see) to occur. Yerushalmi Kiddushin I, 58ᵈ top ולא א׳ מעשה no accident (illegal act) occurred. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 84 כל מה שאירע לזה וכ׳ whatever befell the one, befell also the other; and from—Moʿed Katan II, 1 אֵירְעוֹ אבל (Manuscript Munich אירע בו) mourning in the family befell him; and e.—Yerushalmi Shekalim V, 48ᵈ bottom of page כך וכך אירע; Yerushalmi Demai I, 22ᵃ אירעון … (read אירעוֹ) so and so it happened to him. Part. Pu. מְאוֹרָע see as well

Hithpaël - הִתְאָרֵעַ to be added to, to join. Yerushalmi Sotah I, 17ᵃ אחת מִתְאַרְעָה לאחת וכ׳ one (sin) is added to the other, until the account is full; Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 9.

גּוּף I , perf. and participle גָּף (= גָּפַף) [to join body to body,] to squeeze, cork, bung. Niddah 6ᵇ היתה גָּפָה וכ׳ was corking (pitching) wine jugs. Moʿed Katan 11ᵇ כדו לָגוֹף we take for the mourner his wine jug for corking. [Ib. Mishnah ib. II, 1 וגף, omitted in Manuscript Munich, see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l. note.] Ma'aser Sheni III, 12 אע"פ שגָּפָן; Tosefta ib. II, 18 שגָּפָם (Variant גֹּופָם from גָּפָה) though he corked them; and e.

Piël - גִּיֵּיף to embrace, hug. Yerushalmi Yoma III, 41ᵃ גִּיְּיפוֹ he put his arms around it.

Hifil - הֵגִיף (Nehemiah VII, 3) to fill up (a hole), close (a door), fasten. Parah VI, 1. Oholot XIII, 3 הֵגִיפָהּ ולא וכ׳ he filled the hole out but not entirely. Zavim III, 2 מֵגִיפִין או פותחין if both close or open a door simultaneously. Tosefta Oholot XIV, 1; and e.—Part. pass. מוּגָף fastened. Yerushalmi Ketubot VII, 31ᶜ מ׳ צריכה if the door (behind the suspected couple) was closed (but not locked), it is doubtful (whether the woman is to be considered a Sotah, see סוֹטָה).

זָלַף (compare זלח, דלף)
1) to pour, empty over. Moʿed Katan II, 1, sq. זוֹלֵף וכ׳ he may empty the contents of the vat into the press and finish the process &c. Yerushalmi ib. 81ᵃ bottom of page זוֹלְפִין את יינו they put his grapes for him into the press. Toharot X, 7 הזוֹלֵף את הבור if one empties the wine or oil pit.

—2) to sprinkle. Parah VI, 2 זָלַף וכ׳ (Rabbenu Shimshon זִילֵּף) if he used all the water for sprinkling. Ib. 3 יזלף ed. (comm. זוֹלֵף; Yoma 58ᵃ זולף והולך) he may sprinkle &c. (Bartenura and Rashi to Yoma l. common gender. he may empty the water into bottles &c.). Ib. VII, 8 זולף (Maimonides: he empties &c.); and from

Piël - זִילֵּף to drip, sprinkle. Parah VI, 2, sq., see supra.—Yerushalmi Shabbat IX, 12ᵃ מְזַלְּפִין וכ׳ you may drip hot water on the wound; Tosefta ib. XV (XVI), 4. Shabbat XIX, 3; and e.

Hifil - הִזְלִיף to flow, squirt (neut. verb). Pirkei Avot Zar. 59ᵇ מַזְלִיף (Manuscript Munich מזלף; Tosefta ib. VII (VIII), 5 מנתז).

טעי, טָעָה (Biblical Hebrew)
1) (compare תָּעָה) to err, be mistaken. Berakhot II, 3 קרא וט׳ יחזור למקום שט׳ if in reading the Sh’ma one made a mistake, he must go back to the passage in which he made a mistake. Bava Metzia 63ᵇ בכדי שהדעת טוֹעָה within the limits of a reasonable mistake in counting. Sanhedrin 33ᵇ ט׳ בדבר שהצדוקין וכ׳ if the judge made a mistake in a case in which there is no difference of opinion between the Sadducees and Pharisees. Ib. 6ᵃ, and e. ט׳ בדבר משנה if the judge gave a wrong decision against an explicit law in the Mishnah; ט׳ בשיקול הדעת, see דַּעַת; and from

—2) to seek, to miss (compare טָעַן I). Taanit III, 8 אבן הטוֹעִים; Bava Metzia 28ᵇ אבן טוֹעִין Manuscript Munich (ed. טוֹעַן, see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l. note), see אֶבֶן.—Vayikra Rabbah section (Parashah) 13, beginning אני טָעִיתִי את ההלכה I had forgotten the law in the case.

Hifil - הִטְעָה to lead astray, to deceive, disappoint. Bava Metzia VI, 1 הִטְעוּ זה את זה they deceived one another, i.e. the agent employed to engage laborers did not act according to instruction, see next word—Moʿed Katan II, 1 הִטְעוּהוּ פועלים hired men disappointed him. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 19 end (interpret. hishshiani, Breishit III, 13) הִטְעַנִי he deceived me with false promises; and e.

Hof. - הוּטְעָה to be led astray, be deceived. Midrash Tanḥuma Balak 5 כמו שהטעה ה׳ as he led astray, so was he led astray.—Part. מוּטְעֶה, f. מוּטַעַת, מוּטְעֵית misled, brought about by mistake, under false premises. Yevamot 106ᵃ חליצה מ׳ a ḥălitsah to which the yabam consented in consequence of a deception (a promise not kept); Tosefta ib. XII, 13; Ketubot 74ᵃ.—Rosh Hashanah 25ᵃ אתם אפי׳ מוּטָעִין ‘ye’ (shall appoint), even if deceived by witnesses (your decision stands). Shabbat 101ᵇ מוטעין (mattings fastened, or spread) by mistake; and e.

עֲטִינִים, עֲטִינִין m. plural (עָטַן) packed olives, beginning to drip. Yerushalmi Moʿed Katan II, beginning 81ᵃ מתניתן בע׳ the Mishnah (Moʿed Katan II, 1) speaks of packed olives, opposed גרגרים loose berries.

sections.en: The mishna discusses one who had already turned over his olives as part of the process of preparing them for pressing, and mourning for a close relative befell him and as a result he was prohibited from engaging in work, or some other unavoidable accident occurred, or his workers misled him, promising to come but failing to do so, so that he could not press his olives before the Festival. Under these circumstances, during the intermediate days of the Festival, he may place the olives in the press and load the beam with weights for the initial pressing of the olives and leave it this way until after the Festival; this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda. Rabbi Yosei says: He may press the olives and complete the process and then plug each barrel of oil in its usual manner. Since delay can entail financial loss, the Sages did not require him to alter the normal process of extracting the oil.
sections.he: מִי שֶׁהָפַךְ אֶת זֵיתָיו וְאֵרְעוֹ אֵבֶל אוֹ אֹנֶס, אוֹ שֶׁהִטְעוּהוּ פוֹעֲלִים, טוֹעֵן קוֹרָה רִאשׁוֹנָה וּמַנִּיחָהּ לְאַחַר הַמּוֹעֵד. דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, זוֹלֵף וְגוֹמֵר וְגָף כְּדַרְכּוֹ:

en:
לִימּוּדִים, לִימּוּדִין, לִמּ׳ m. plural (לָמַד) [junctions,]
1) mortised shingles or boards used as frames. Kelim V, 9 תנור … ועשה לו ל׳ an oven which came in parts from the workshop and which (after being put up) was surrounded with a frame. Ib. סלק את לִימּוּדָיו ed. Dehr. (oth. ed. לִמּ׳) if the frame was removed; Tosefta Kelim Bava Kamma IV, 12. Ib. VII, 9 עין של תנור … ל׳ וכ׳ a chimney-flue which is lined with boards. Tosefta Pesachim VII, 1; Moʿed Katan II, 2 עושה לו ל׳ וכ׳ he makes a frame of shingles and covers the vat that the wine may not get sour; and e.

—2) a sort of common bread, ‘shingles’. Tosefta Hallah I, 7; Yerushalmi ib. I, end, 58ᵃ עשאה ל׳ פטורה if he made the ‘dog’s dough’, into ‘shingles’, it is exempt (from Ḥallah); Berakhot 38ᵃ כל׳ ed.; see כַּעַךְ.

sections.en: And similarly, with regard to one whose wine was already in the collection pit beside the wine press and needed to be removed lest it sour, and mourning for some close relative or some other unavoidable accident befell him, or his workers misled him, promising to come but failing to do so, during the intermediate days of the Festival he may draw off the wine and complete the process, and then plug each barrel of wine in its usual manner; this is the statement of Rabbi Yosei. Rabbi Yehuda says: He should construct a wooden panel to cover the collection pit so that the wine will not sour.
sections.he: וְכֵן מִי שֶׁהָיָה יֵינוֹ בְּתוֹךְ הַבּוֹר וְאֵרְעוֹ אֵבֶל אוֹ אֹנֶס, אוֹ שֶׁהִטְעוּהוּ פוֹעֲלִים, זוֹלֵף וְגוֹמֵר וְגָף כְּדַרְכּוֹ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, עוֹשֶׂה לוֹ לִמּוּדִים, בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁלֹּא יַחְמִיץ:

en:
שלי, שָׁלָה I (Biblical Hebrew; Job XXVII, 8) to draw out, pull. Taanit 24ᵃ; Shabbat 107ᵇ השׁוֹלֶה דג וכ׳ he that takes a fish out of the water (on the Sabbath). Chullin 63ᵃ (explained שָׁלָךְ, Vayikra XI, 17) זה השולה דגים וכ׳ that is the bird that catches fish out of the sea. Moʿed Katan II, 3 ושולה פשתנו וכ׳ and may take his flax out of the pond. Yalkut Kohelet 966 אדם שוקע … שולה ראשון if one sinks pots into his furnace, he takes out first what he has last put in; and from—[Yerushalmi Ma'aser Sheni III, 53ᶜ top שולה, read: שורה, see שָׁרָה.]

Piël - שִׁילָּה same, especially to draw wine (out of the pit). Pirkei Avot Zar. 56ᵃ; Bava Metzia 92ᵇ היין … משׁיְשַׁלֶּה בחביות wine is subject to tithes …, when he fills it into kegs; Yerushalmi Terumot II, 41ᵇ bottom of page משישלה ומשיקפה (not משיקיפה) when he has filled and skimmed it; עד שלא שי׳ וכ׳ before he filled or skimmed it. Tosefta Ma'asrot I, 7 המקדיש … עד שלא שילה וקיפה מששילה וקיפה וכ׳ (ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) שולה וקופה וכ׳, correct accordingly) if one dedicates the contents of a pit before he has drawn and skimmed the wine, and the Temple collector comes after he has done so &c.; and e.

Nifal - נִשְׁלֶה to be pulled, drawn away. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 22, beginning (reference. to Breishit IV, 1) ידע מאיזו שלוה נ׳ he knew from what happiness he was drawn away (through his wife).

comments.en: but you must also pull some [stalks] out of the heaps and leave them for her to glean, and not scold her.”
comments.he: וְגַ֛ם שֹׁל־תָּשֹׁ֥לּוּ לָ֖הּ מִן־הַצְּבָתִ֑ים וַעֲזַבְתֶּ֥ם וְלִקְּטָ֖ה וְלֹ֥א תִגְעֲרוּ־בָֽהּ׃

sections.en: A person may bring his fruit in from the field on the intermediate days of the Festival because he is concerned about thieves, and he may draw his flax out of the soaking pool so that it is not ruined from soaking too long in the water, provided that he does not plan from the outset to perform his work on the intermediate days of the Festival. And with regard to all of these cases, if one planned from the outset to perform his labor on the intermediate days of the Festival, the fruit of that labor must be lost and no benefit may be derived from it.
sections.he: מַכְנִיס אָדָם פֵּרוֹתָיו מִפְּנֵי הַגַּנָּבִים, וְשׁוֹלֶה פִשְׁתָּנוֹ מִן הַמִּשְׁרָה בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁלֹּא תֹאבַד, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יְכַוֵּן אֶת מְלַאכְתּוֹ בַמּוֹעֵד. וְכֻלָּן אִם כִּוְּנוּ מְלַאכְתָּן בַּמּוֹעֵד, יֹאבֵדוּ:

en: צוֹרֶךְ, צֹרֶךְ m. (Biblical Hebrew; צָרַךְ) need, necessity. Moʿed Katan II, 4 לצ׳ המועד if required for use during the festival; לצ׳ המוכר if the seller is in need of money. Pesachim 5ᵇ we do not say, הואיל והותרה … לצ׳ … שלא לצ׳ since lighting a fire is permitted (on the Holy Day) for the need of the day, it may also be permitted where it is not needed for the day. Yerushalmi Nazir III, beginning 54ᶜ הבערה לצ׳ יצאת the prohibition to start a fire on the Sabbath (Shemot XXXV, 3) is specified for a purpose (for interpretation). Shabbat 131ᵇ צ׳ גבוה needed for the altar (see גָּבוֹהַּ). Beitzah 21ᵇ עושה אדם כל צָרְכוֹ בפת man may use a loaf of bread for whatever he may need (not only for eating); Berakhot 50ᵇ צָרְכָיו (plural). Sanhedrin 88ᵇ שלא שמשו כל צָרְכָן who had not attended their teachers sufficiently; Yerushalmi ib. I, 19ᶜ כצוֹרְכָן; and see from—Euphemisms: Yerushalmi Ketubot V, 30ᵇ היתה עושה צוֹרְכָהּ באחרים she gratified her desire with other men; Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 52 צָרָכֶיהָ (plural). Yerushalmi Berakhot III, 6ᶜ אעשה צָרְכִי I will gratify my desire; and from—plural צֳרָכִים, constr. צוֹרְכֵי, צָרְכֵי. Berakhot 46ᵇ צ׳ סעודה the requirements of a meal. Shabbat XIX, 2 (133ᵃ, sq.) כל צ׳ מילה all preparations needed for circumcision. Shekalim IV, 7 ימכרו לצ׳ עולות (Yerushalmi ed. לצְרִיכֵי) shall be sold for the purposes of (to buy with the money realized) burnt-offerings. Beitzah 28ᵇ לכם לכל צָרְכֵיכֶם ‘for you’ (Shemot XII, 16), for all your needs of the day. Yerushalmi Berakhot V, 9ᵇ bottom of page שואל צָרְכָיו וכ׳ inserts the prayer for his individual needs in the benediction ‘Hearer of Prayers’. Vayikra Rabbah section (Parashah) 34, end (reference. to Isaiah LVIII, 13) מכאן … לתבוע צרכיו בשבת from this we learn that man must not pray for his individual wants on the Sabbath; and from—Yerushalmi Chagigah II, 78ᵃ top עשה צרכיו עמה had marital connection with her, see supra. Niddah IX, 1 עושה צרכיה urinated. Ib. 2 צָרְכֵיהֶן. Yalkut Job 927 (reference. to Job XLI, 7) סוגר כל חותמות הצרכים he (the Leviathan) closes all the seals of needs (all his own orifices of discharge, contradistinguished to כל חותמות המְצָרְכִים all the seals of those that have needs (causes their obstruction); and from

sections.en: One may not purchase houses, slaves, and cattle on the intermediate days of a Festival unless it is for the sake of the Festival, or to provide for the needs of the seller who does not have anything to eat. One may not move his possessions from house to house during the intermediate days of a Festival, but he may move them to his courtyard if that is necessary. One may not bring home utensils from the house of a craftsman after he has completed his work, but if one is concerned about them that if he leaves them in the craftsman’s house they are likely to be stolen, he may move them to another courtyard.
sections.he: אֵין לוֹקְחִין בָּתִּים, עֲבָדִים וּבְהֵמָה, אֶלָּא לְצֹרֶךְ הַמּוֹעֵד, אוֹ לְצֹרֶךְ הַמּוֹכֵר, שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מַה יֹּאכָל. אֵין מְפַנִּין מִבַּיִת לְבַיִת, אֲבָל מְפַנֶּה הוּא לַחֲצֵרוֹ. אֵין מְבִיאִין כֵּלִים מִבֵּית הָאֻמָּן. וְאִם חוֹשֵׁשׁ לָהֶם, מְפַנָּן לְחָצֵר אַחֶרֶת:

en:
דָּרַשׁ (Biblical Hebrew)
1) to examine, question. Denom. דְּרִישָׁה.

—2) to expound, interpret. Berakhot I, 5 עד שדְּרָשָׁהּ בן זומא until Ben Zoma found an intimation of it in the Biblical wording. Taanit 5ᵇ מקרא אני דוֹרֵשׁ I find it intimated in a Bible verse. Bava Metzia 104ᵃ היה ד׳ לשון הדיוט interpreted the popular (Chaldaic) wording used in documents. Pesachim 22ᵇ, see אֵת; and see from—Part. pass. דָּרוּשׁ, f. דְּרוּשָׁה. Yerushalmi Yevamot VIII, 8ᵈ top והלא ד׳ הוא has not the word ממנו been employed for interpretation?, opposed מופנה.—Denom. דְּרִישָׁה, מִדְרָשׁ.

—3) (in gen.) to teach, lecture. Chagigah II, 1 אין דֹּורְשִׁין ב־ you must not lecture on &c. Sanhedrin 99ᵇ ודורש בהגדות וכ׳ lectured on topics with the object of fault-finding; and see from—דֹּורֵשׁ lecturer. Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 42, beginning אבא הַדֹּ׳ Abba, the lecturer. Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 8, end, see אֲמוֹרָא.—plural דֹּורְשִׁים. Sanhedrin 38ᵇ; Pirkei Avot Zar. 5ᵃ דור דור ודוֹרְשָׁיו every generation with its preachers. דֹּורְשֵׁי חמורות, see חוֹמֶר; ד׳ רשומות, see רְשׁוּמָה. [Moʿed Katan II, 5 (13ᵇ) דורשין Manuscript Munich (ed. עושין), read דֹּושְׁשִׁין.]

Nifal - נִדְרַשׁ to be interpreted, expounded. Sifra, introduction rules שהתורה נִדְרֶשֶׁת בהן by which the Law is interpreted. Yerushalmi Peah II, 17ᵃ דברים הַנִּדְרָשִׁין מן הכתב things which are derived by interpretation from the written code (Torah); הנדרשין מן הפה derived from the oral code (Mishnah). Yerushalmi Megillah I, 70ᵃ top נתנה להִידָּרֵשׁ is a legitimate object of interpretation.

Hithpaël - הִתְדָּרֵשׁ same. Yerushalmi Ketubot III, 27ᵈ top מִתְדָּרֵשׁ (מִתְדָּרְשָׁה) ולו וכ׳ the words v’lo &c. are open for interpretation, see גְּזֵרָה.

דָּשֹׁושׁ m. , plural דָּשֹׁושֹׁות (compare דָּרוֹכוֹת) wheat-stampers, groats-makers. Moʿed Katan II, 5 (13ᵇ; Manuscript רששות, רשתות, see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l.).—Constr. דָּשֹׁושֵׁי. Ib. 13ᵇ ed. (Manuscript ר׳). V. דָּשַׁשׁ.

סְמַךְ I, סְמֵיךְ Chaldaic same
1) to press, lay hands on, lean on. Targum Amos V, 19. Targum Shemot XXIX, 10; and from

—2) to support, uphold. Targum Psalms LI, 14; and e.

—3) to rest on; to rely, feel safe. Targum Sheni (to Esther) Samuel I, 6. Targum Psalms LXXXVIII, 8. Ib. LXXI, 6; andfr. from—Chagigah 20ᵇ מִיסְמַךְ סָמְכָא דעתייהו their mind is at rest (they feel safe that they cannot be seen). Pirkei Avot Zar. 71ᵇ סמכא דעתיה he feels sure (of his bargain); and from

—4) to bring close, join. Yerushalmi Shabbat III, 5ᵈ bottom of page, see אֲדֵירָא. Yevamot 119ᵃ סְמוֹךְ מיעוטא וכ׳ bring close, i.e. add. &c., see מִיעוּטָא; Kiddushin 80ᵃ; and e.—Esp. to ordain (see preceding, and Targum Devarim XXXIV, 9). Sanhedrin 13ᵇ (explained סמיכת זקנים, see סְמִיכוּת) מִיסְמַךְ סבי ordaining of elders. Ib. בירֹא ממש סַמְכִין ליה או בשמא סמכין ליה Manuscript Munich must they ordain him by actually putting a hand on him, or merely by calling his name? Ib. וחד לא סָמֵיךְ and one alone cannot ordain? Ib. 14ᵃ ור"מ … סַמְכֵיה was it R. J. ben B. that ordained R. Meir? Ib. הוה מיטמר מלמיסמכיה Manuscript Munich was on his guard not to be ordained. Ib. סְמוֹכוּ לנא appoint for us as teachers, see חֲמִיסִין; and from—Part. pass. סָמִיךְ, סְמִיךְ a) ordained. Pesachim 49ᵃ תרי בני סְמִיכֵי two sons both of whom were ordained teachers.—b) near, adjoining. Targum Yonatan I Bamidbar XXI, 14. Ib. II, 5; 12, and e. (interch. with סְמוּכִין). Targum Yonatan Devarim VI, 7.—Sanhedrin 7ᵇ וס׳ ליה וכ׳ and next to it follows &c.; ib. 107ᵃ; and from

Pa. - סַמֵּךְ
1) to press, stamp, make a thick mass. Pesachim 116ᵃ וצריך לסַמּוּכֵיה וכ׳ and you must make it a thick mass so as to be emblematical of clay (see חֲרוֹסֶת).

—2) to secure, especially to refer to a depositary for payment; to draw an order for. Yerushalmi Kiddushin III, 64ᵃ top סַמְּכֵיה גבי לוי he referred him to Levy (as his depositary). Ib. סַמְּכוּן … גבי זבונה they secured the teacher by a deposit with a merchant. Yerushalmi Shevuot VII, 38ᵃ top, כַּתָּפָא. Yerushalmi Bava Metzia IV, beginning 9ᶜ; and e.

Af. - אַסְמַךְ
1) to give an order to. Ib. אנא בעי … דאַסְמִיכְתַּנִי I want to collect the money for which thou hast given me an order (at the banker’s).

—2) to lean on; to find support; to give support. Yerushalmi Berakhot II, 4ᶜ כל מילה … מַסְמְכִין לה מן וכ׳ whenever a proposition is not evident, they try to support it by a large number of Biblical passages; Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 22 מַסְמְכִינָן, see אֲתַר. Moʿed Katan 5ᵃ אַסְמְכָהּ אקרא gave it support by reference to a Biblical verse. Berakhot 19ᵇ כל מילי … אַסְמְכִינְהוּ על וכ׳ they lean all rules of the Rabbis on the law, ‘Thou shalt not deviate’, see סוּר I; and e.

—3) to make substantial, put a thick layer on. Moʿed Katan 13ᵇ מעבין אַסְמוּכֵי mʾʿabbin (Mishnah ib. II, 5) means covering with a heavy layer, opposed אַקְלוּשֵׁי, see קְלַשׁ.

Ithpeel - אִסְתְּמִיךְ to lean; to rely. Targum Judges XVI, 26. Targum Isaiah L, 10; and from—Yevamot 42ᵇ מִסְתְּמִיךְ ואזיל וכ׳ R. A. walked leaning on the shoulder of &c. Yerushalmi Berakhot II, 4ᵇ; Yerushalmi Moʿed Katan III, 83ᶜ bottom of page ר׳ יוחנן הוה מיסתמיך וכ׳ R. J. was (walking) leaning on &c.; and from

עבי, עָבָה (Biblical Hebrew; compare עָבַב) to be thick, dense, dark.

Nifal - נֶעֱבֶה to become thick, swell. Midrash Tanḥuma Vaëra 3 ובלען … ולא נ׳ יותר וכ׳ Aaron’s staff swallowed them up and yet was not thicker than before.

Hifil - הֶעֱבָה same. Tosefta Kilayim III, 4 הֶעֱבוּ ונעשו מכוונות (not העבן) if the plants on growing denser appeared to form a straight line; Yerushalmi ib. V, beginning 29ᵈ העבות (Rabbenu Shimshon to Kilayim V, 1 היו עבים; correct accordingly).

Piël - עִיבָּה to make thick; to condense, darken; to facilitate growth. Yerushalmi Taanit III, 66ᶜ מְעַבֶּה, see עָב II. Moʿed Katan II, 5 מְחַפִּין … אף מְעַבִּין (during the festive week) you may cover up the cut figs with straw; … you may even &c.; explained ib. 13ᵇ מחפין אקלושי מעבין אסמוכי by m’ḥappin is meant a loose covering, by m’ʿabbin a dense, packed covering; (anoth. opinion) מחפין … מע׳ … כמין כרי m’ḥappin means a loose or a dense covering, m’ʿabbin means bringing the figs close together so as to form a pile. Yerushalmi Peah III, 17ᶜ בשעי׳ על מנת להדל if he set the plants close together with the intention of thinning them afterwards. Ib. VII, 20ᵇ מתוך שהוא מְעַבָּן וכ׳ because he strengthens the remaining plants (by thinning the field), they produce more fruit the next year (and thus he benefits also the poor). Yerushalmi Sheviit I, beginning 33ᵃ מעבה את הכורת he advances the growth of the ramification, opposed מתיש כוחה. Yerushalmi Beitzah IV, 62ᶜ top בשלא נתכוין לעַבֹּותָהּ when (in putting wood on the booth) he had not had the intention to cover it more densely; and e.—Tosefta Peah IV, 14 המעבה את שוקיו (ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) המקפח) he who contracts his shoulders (simulating a hump), see קָפַח.—Part. pass. מְעוּבֶּה, see as well

קְלַשׁ (compare קלף) to plane, make thin, weaken. Eruvin 3ᵃ אמרינן קְלוֹשׁ we say, plane it, i.e. consider it reduced to a fine film. Ib. אי קַלְשַׁה if thou makest it very thin. Nedarim 68ᵃ מִיקְלַשׁ קָלֵישׁ does he plane (weaken) it?, see גּוּז Chaldaic—Part. pass. קָלִישׁ, קְלִישָׁא; f. קְלִישָׁא, קְלִישְׁתָּא thin, weak. Targum Yonatan Bamidbar VII, 13 (ed. Vienna קַלִּישָׁא); ib. 19 (opposed סמיך); and e.—Taanit 9ᵇ עיבא ק׳ a light cloud, opposed סמיכתא. Sotah 34ᵇ איידי דק׳ ארעא because the layer of earth (over the rocky soil) is very light. Yevamot 113ᵃ bottom of page דעתא ק׳ וכ׳ his reason is weak, but it is doubtful whether it is equally clear &c., see צִילָא; ib. 113ᵇ. Sukkah 48ᵇ חמרא סמיך מיא ק׳ wine is thick (does nor run out quickly), water is thin.

Af. - אַקְלֵישׁ to make thin, cover with a thin layer. Moʿed Katan 13ᵇ מחפין אַקְלוּשֵׁי m’ḥappin (Mishnah ib. II, 5) means covering lightly, opposed אסמוכי.

Ithpeel - אִתְקְלִישׁ
1) to become thin, lean. Targum Yonatan Breishit XXI, 15.

—2) to become smooth of surface. Targum Job XXXIII, 25 Regia (ed. אתחליש).

רָשׁוֹשׁ m. (רָשַׁשׁ) wheat-stamper, groats-maker.—plural רָשׁוֹשׁוֹת, constr. רָשׁוֹשֵׁי. Moʿed Katan II, 5 (13ᵇ, see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l. note 70). Ib. 13ᵇ ר׳ ציפורי; see דָּשׁוֹשׁ.

sections.en: On the intermediate days of a Festival, figs that were spread out to dry may be covered with straw to protect them from rain and dew. Rabbi Yehuda says: One may even condense the figs. Those who sell produce, clothing, and utensils may sell them in private, for the sake of the Festival. Fishermen, and groats makers [dashoshot], and bean pounders, who pulverize the beans, may ply their trades in private for the sake of the Festival. Rabbi Yosei says: They were stringent with themselves to refrain from this work even with respect to what was needed for the Festival.
sections.he: מְחַפִּין אֶת הַקְּצִיעוֹת בְּקַשׁ. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף מְעַבִּין. מוֹכְרֵי פֵרוֹת, כְּסוּת וְכֵלִים, מוֹכְרִים בְּצִנְעָה לְצֹרֶךְ הַמּוֹעֵד. הַצַּיָּדִין וְהַדָּשׁוֹשׁוֹת וְהַגָּרוֹסוֹת, עוֹשִׂין בְּצִנְעָה לְצֹרֶךְ הַמּוֹעֵד. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, הֵם הֶחְמִירוּ עַל עַצְמָן:
